guide.title: Dose & Simple Calculations
guide.lead: Most drug errors are maths errors. Convert to kilograms and the same units first, use one formula – what you want, divided by what you have, times what it's in – and check the answer makes sense before you draw it up.

steps.title: Units first
steps.text: 1 g = 1000 mg; 1 mg = 1000 mcg. Pounds ÷ 2.2 = kg.

steps.title: Volume
steps.text: Volume = dose wanted ÷ concentration (what you have per mL).

steps.title: Sense check
steps.text: Is the volume reasonable? A tiny or huge volume usually means a units or decimal error.

steps.title: Example
steps.text: 500 mL over 4 hours with a 15 drops/mL set = 500 × 15 ÷ 240 ≈ 31 drops/min.

steps.title: Microdrip shortcut
steps.text: With 60 drops/mL tubing, drops/min equals mL/hour.

sections.title: Children
items: Use a measured or length-based weight; never guess
Check against the maximum adult dose
Small volumes: use a 1 mL syringe

flashcards.question: Dose formula
flashcards.answer: Volume = dose wanted ÷ concentration. (What you want ÷ what you have × what it's in.)

flashcards.question: Microdrip shortcut
flashcards.answer: With 60 drops/mL tubing, drops/min = mL/hour: 125 mL/hour = 125 drops/min.

flashcards.question: 40 lb child, 5 mg/kg
flashcards.answer: 40 ÷ 2.2 = 18.2 kg; × 5 = about 91 mg. Always convert to kg first.

flashcards.question: Length-based tape
flashcards.answer: Estimates a child's weight from length when no scale is available, with pre-calculated doses.

critical.scenario: 5-year-old seizing for 8 minutes; mother says he weighs 40 lb. Protocol: midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IN (maximum 10 mg); vial 5 mg/mL.
critical.question: Dose and volume?

options.t: 40 ÷ 2.2 ≈ 18 kg; 18 × 0.2 = 3.6 mg; 3.6 ÷ 5 = 0.72 mL, split between nostrils

critical.explanation: Confirm the weight against a length-based tape.
critical.kpi: Calculates a weight-based pediatric dose correctly

critical.scenario: 70 kg adult, dehydrated and hypotensive. Protocol: 20 mL/kg bolus. 15 drops/mL set; over 1 hour.
critical.question: Volume and drip rate?

options.t: 70 × 20 = 1400 mL; 1400 × 15 ÷ 60 = 350 drops/min – too fast to count; run wide open or use a pressure bag and reassess

critical.explanation: Reassess lungs and blood pressure after each portion.
critical.kpi: Calculates fluid volume and infusion rate

critical.scenario: Your partner asks for ondansetron 4 mg. New vials are labelled 4 mg/2 mL; you drew up 4 mL thinking it was 1 mg/mL.
critical.question: What failed and how do you prevent it?

options.t: Concentration was misread (it's 2 mg/mL, so 4 mg is 2 mL). Read the concentration at every check, say it aloud, recalculate, and report the near miss

critical.explanation: Changes in stock are a known error trap: tell the whole team.
critical.kpi: Identifies concentration-reading errors and prevention strategies
